items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Jimmy Johnson stayed sick for about six months. And he'd be okay, okay, come up and play with us.

ctx.x: Vic, I played with Vic. Who was I with when I played with Vic? I believe Manuel Key come up on the roof corner and played with a Suiv. Jimmy Johnson stayed sick for about six months. And he'd be okay, okay, come up and play with us.
What about Udel? Well he was a nice piano player. I never worked with him. Did he work with bands all along?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: And they sent to St. Louis and got Kimberl Dial and Jimmy Johnson, bass and alto.

ctx.x: Who was the manager of that Georgia Minstrel? Do you remember anything else about the company? Who else was in the band?

Well, I didn't know nobody in the band but Kimberl Dial. He the one gave me the job because he played with us on the boat after Elliot Taylor taking sick. They sent to St. Louis and got him and the guys, Simon, taking sick too. Simon Moreira taking sick on the boat. And they sent to St. Louis and got Kimberl Dial and Jimmy Johnson, bass and alto. So Kimberl was the only guy that I knew on the show. Yeah. I didn't know none of the musicians. I didn't know. Just got quaming with him afterwards, you know.

items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: And Jimmy John, Simon was on bass. It's time to take him sick.

ctx.x: And Jimmy John, Simon was on bass. It's time to take him sick. Then we got a guy out of St. Louis, Jimmy, Jimmy Jones. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I mean, them guys couldn't play. Peter Hunter, I told you. You know what happened? Set them David Horn on the left. He stayed out in the hour. Yeah.
He went on to say, huh?
